Explore the relationship between search radius and neighborhood size

Source: R/Explore_Radius_Neighborhood.R
Explore_Radius_Neighborhood.Rd

Estimates the mean number of neighboring cells as a function of search radius, using a randomly sampled subset of cells for efficiency. Designed to help users choose a radius parameter before calling create_NICHESObject().

Usage

Explore_Radius_Neighborhood(
  coord,
  r.min = NULL,
  r.max = NULL,
  r.step = NULL,
  n.sample = 2000L,
  seed = 42L,
  n.cores = 1L,
  show.plot = TRUE
)

Arguments

coord

data.frame. First two columns must be numeric x and y coordinates. Row names must be unique cell barcodes.

r.min

numeric(1). Minimum radius to evaluate. Default: 1% of the bounding-box diagonal.

r.max

numeric(1). Maximum radius to evaluate. Default: 20% of the bounding-box diagonal.

r.step

numeric(1). Step size between evaluated radii. Default: (r.max - r.min) / 50 (50 evenly spaced evaluation points).

n.sample

integer(1) or NULL. Number of cells to randomly sample for the neighborhood estimate. Default 2000. Set to NULL to use all cells – not recommended for large datasets.

seed

integer(1) or NULL. Random seed for reproducible sampling. Default 42. The caller's random number state is restored on exit.

n.cores

integer(1). Number of parallel workers (socket cluster) for distributing the radius evaluation. Default 1.

show.plot

logical. Whether to print the summary ggplot before returning. Default TRUE.

Value

A data.table with columns:

radius

evaluated radius value

mean.neighbors

mean neighbor count across sampled cells

sd.neighbors

standard deviation of neighbor count

median.neighbors

median neighbor count (robust to density outliers)

Returned invisibly when show.plot = TRUE.

Details

A single kd-tree query via dbscan::frNN() is run at r.max; all smaller radii are evaluated by thresholding the already-retrieved distance lists, so the kd-tree is built only once regardless of how many radius steps are requested.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_inputs)

# Build a coord data.frame from the example metadata
coord <- NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data[, c("x", "y")]
rownames(coord) <- rownames(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data)

# Sweep radius across the bounding box; small dataset -> use all 80 cells
radius.curve <- Explore_Radius_Neighborhood(
  coord     = coord,
  n.sample  = 80L,
  n.cores   = 1L,
  show.plot = FALSE
)
head(radius.curve)
#>        radius mean.neighbors sd.neighbors median.neighbors
#>         <num>          <num>        <num>            <num>
#> 1: 0.01317801          0.100    0.3765264                0
#> 2: 0.01828785          0.200    0.5372221                0
#> 3: 0.02339769          0.350    0.7647288                0
#> 4: 0.02850753          0.525    0.8711261                0
#> 5: 0.03361737          0.675    0.9246963                0
#> 6: 0.03872721          0.775    0.9933322                1
# }
